component.name: Argent Forge
component.summary: Doom editor, a fork of SLADE3

description.p: Argent Forge is a fork of SLADE3, the editor for Doom-engine games and source ports written by Simon Judd. It opens WADs, PK3s and the rest of the formats those games use, draws and converts their graphics, and edits the maps.

On top of SLADE it adds a visual actor constructor that reads and writes your DECORATE and ZScript without rewriting what it did not touch, a menu constructor that edits a mod's MENUDEF with a live preview of the menu as the game draws it, a sprite preview beside the code editor, painting tools for the picture editor, and two colour schemes of its own.
Everything from SLADE that this fork did not change is still SLADE's, and upstream releases are not updates to this build.

ul.li: A LANGUAGE file written as a spreadsheet, the shape a modern port uses for itself, opens in the Language Constructor: one line per string and one column per language.
For such a file the Additional button asks which languages of it to put on the screen, since one file holds thirty of them at once.
A language the file leaves as an empty field shows the source text quietly, which is the table saying it isn't translated.
A table of two thousand lines redraws in a tenth of a second instead of fourteen seconds.
The Language Constructor: edit a mod's LANGUAGE lumps as a table of one column per file, and paint part of a string with the colours the engine itself reads.
A new translation comes with its $key written for you, and an untranslated value sits grey in the column until it is.
The table and the code editor follow each other: pick a row and the editor moves to its line, pick a line and the row lights up.
The Menu Constructor reads a block you select as one run, so rows move, copy, paste and delete together, and its buttons appear only over the lump they belong to.
Preferences has a Language Constructor page and an Integration page for the SLADE import and AceZDL settings.
Holding SHIFT over a sprite name plays the states you selected as one animation, and can follow a 'goto' into the state it names.
The preview says which state each picture belongs to, and holds each frame for its real length instead of drifting behind it.
Two Actor Constructor settings show the value you saved rather than coming up empty and resetting it.
A window that had been closed minimized, or on a monitor that has since gone, no longer comes back where nobody can see it.
The Menu Constructor: edit a mod's menus from the text that is open, with a preview that draws them the way the game does.
Its lists come from your own archive: cvars, TEXTCOLO ranges, LANGUAGE labels, pictures, and the widget classes a mod writes in its own ZScript.
An empty MENUDEF is a starting point now: the window asks where your first menu should hang and writes both blocks it takes to be seen in game.
Open Containing Folder for projects opened as folders, and a setting that hands Argent Forge to AceZDL.
Settings live in Argent Forge's own folder, with a one-time import of SLADE's.
